captions.text: Numbering helps people connect an item with its operational process.
In our Chicago Fire demonstration department, calls, records and
work orders have separate settings.
From Department Settings, open Calls & Dispatch, then Call Settings for calls.
Document Numbering is under Customization.
For records, open Records, expand Manage and choose Settings.
Work orders, invoices, bids and daily time reports share Document Numbering.
Check the page before editing: saving an invoice pattern does not change
call or incident-record numbering.

instruction_review.method: All27 actual complete JPEGs viewed with exact frozen speech. Literal controls mapped to pictured viewports, including new Document Numbering Update shot. Three internal cuts use genuine one-second export anchors; no estimated timing. Old and new counter scopes and saved/preview states are kept distinct.

captions.text: Open Call Settings and scroll to Call Numbering.
Our saved pattern is FD51-{YYYY}-{SEQ}: a department prefix, full year and sequence.
Sequence digits is four.
The inline example uses sample sequence 153, so it reads FD51-2026-0153; that
sample is not the next issued number.
The sequence token must appear exactly once.
Letters, digits and supported separators form the fixed text.
Review the example, choose Update and reopen the page to check the stored
format before creating a training call.

captions.text: Read the token guidance under Call number pattern.
A year pattern restarts each numbering year.
Adding month makes a monthly scope; adding day makes a daily scope.
A month needs a year, and a day needs a month.
Without a date, the sequence continues without a date-based restart.
For example, AC-{YYYY}{MM}{DD}-{SEQ} is a daily format.
We keep the saved yearly FD51 pattern here.
Dates follow the department time zone, so check that setting
before choosing a reset rule.

captions.text: Review Numbering year starts.
Our saved month is January and the day is one, so this example
follows the calendar year.
A yearly format starts a new sequence at its numbering-year boundary.
Before using a different boundary, review the intended year label and the page's
help against your department's convention.
Monthly and daily call patterns use calendar dates.
We are leaving the fiscal settings unchanged and checking
the displayed next number.

Saving our new FD51 format started its own scope at 0001; older

After the training call received 0001, this page shows 0002.
Raise next sequence to is for carrying forward numbers issued before Resgrid.
It can only move forward.
Save pattern or year-boundary changes first, reopen, then review any separate
carry-forward value against the new scope.

captions.text: In an authorized training exercise, open the saved call and compare its issued
number with the format you reviewed.
Our disposable training call received FD51-2026-0001.
An older call keeps its original 26-format number because a pattern
change never rewrites issued numbers.
Mixed historical formats can therefore be expected.
If a result differs from what you expected, check the local date,
numbering-year boundary and scope.
Do not create repeated calls merely to force a counter toward the inline sample.

captions.text: In Records Settings, find Record numbering.
We preserve {PREFIX}-{YYYY}-{SEQ}
with four digits and January first.
PREFIX uses the record type prefix.
Training defaults to TRN when its override box is blank.
The next-number table shows TRN-2026-0002 after the existing training record.
Prefixes shared by types share a sequence; GROUP can create group-specific scopes
and must be followed by a separator.
Calls month and day tokens do not belong here.
Review stored settings and each relevant next row before
changing this separate family.

scenes.title: Verify a record and its scope

captions.text: Open the existing training record.
Its issued number is TRN-2026-0001, its station is Firehouse 51
and its state is Finalized.
The register also has a separate Work draft with a draft reference.
These are different types and lifecycle states.
A number identifies an item; it does not by itself establish review,
approval or external submission.
Check the state and history separately.
Use an existing safe example when one is available, preserving its
original contents and audit trail.

Each row controls work orders, invoices, bids or daily time reports.

saved next value initially read 0001.
After the request was issued, it advanced to MNT-26-0002.
Invoice, bid and time-report rows retain their built-in formats.
This page has its own numbering-year boundary, separate from Calls and Records.
Reopen after saving and inspect every row you intended to change.
